cards.text: Pull up a stool, friend. The word of the LORD comes to Jonah son of Amittai, a prophet from Gath-hepher (2 Kings 14:25). And this is NOT small talk.
God tells Jonah to get up, go to the great city of Nineveh, and preach against it. Big city. BIG job.

cards.question: God is sending Jonah to preach against Nineveh. What reason does God give?

answers.text: Its wickedness has come up before Him
Its king has turned his back on Him
Its people have mocked all His prophets

cards.question: Jonah gets up and heads straight for Nineveh, just like God said.

cards.text: Nope. Jonah gets up to flee from the presence of the LORD, goes down to Joppa, and finds a ship, which is like your boss calling with a big job and you buying a plane ticket instead of picking up.

cards.question: Jonah has found a ship at Joppa. Where is it bound?

cards.text: So Jonah pays the fare and sails off, away from the presence of the LORD. Friend, the man PAID to run from God.

cards.question: With Jonah out at sea, the LORD hurls a great ___ upon the sea.

cards.text: Such a violent storm comes up that the ship is in danger of breaking apart. I spent YEARS in a junk drawer, friend, and even I'd rather be back in there than on that boat.

cards.question: The sailors are afraid, and each one cries out to his own god.
Next, the sailors throw something into the sea to lighten the load. What is it?
While the sailors work up top, Jonah has gone down to the lowest part of the ship, where he lies down in a deep ___.

cards.text: ASLEEP. The ship's in danger of breaking apart, the sailors are crying out to their gods, and Jonah is down there like he hit the snooze button on a hurricane.

cards.question: The captain comes to Jonah and tells him to get up and call upon his God.

cards.text: The captain says, “Perhaps this God will consider us, so that we may not perish.” Friend, when the captain has to come wake YOU up to pray, it is not your day.
Back up top, the sailors want to find out who's responsible for this calamity. Everybody's looking at everybody.

cards.question: How do the sailors find out who's responsible for the storm?
The sailors cast lots, and the lot falls on Jonah.

cards.text: Of COURSE it lands on Jonah. Now the sailors fire off five questions about who's to blame, his work, where he's from, his country and his people, like a job interview in the middle of a storm.

cards.question: Jonah tells the sailors he's a Hebrew who worships the LORD. How does he describe the LORD?

answers.text: The God who made the sea and the dry land
The God who rules from the temple in Jerusalem
The God who led Israel out of the land of Egypt

cards.text: Hold up. Jonah is running from the God who made the sea, and his getaway plan is a BOAT.

cards.question: The sailors know Jonah is fleeing from the presence of the LORD, because he told them. Now they're even more ___.

cards.text: “What have you done?” they ask him. Meanwhile, the sea keeps growing worse and worse.

cards.question: The sailors ask Jonah what they must do to him to calm the sea. Jonah tells them to throw him into the sea.

cards.text: Then Jonah says, “For I know that I am to blame for this violent storm that has come upon you.” Give the man this much: he owns it.

cards.question: Jonah has told the sailors to throw him into the sea. What do they do first?

answers.text: They row hard to get back to land
They tie Jonah to the mast
They cast lots a second time

cards.text: They row HARD to get back to dry land, but the sea rages against them more and more.

cards.question: Out of options, the sailors cry out to the LORD. What do they ask Him?

answers.text: Not to charge them with innocent blood
To carry them safely on to Tarshish
To forgive them for casting the lots

cards.question: The sailors pick Jonah up and cast him into the sea, and the sea keeps on raging.

cards.text: Calm. Friend, I've waited longer for an oven to cool off.

cards.question: With the sea calm, the men ___ the LORD greatly and make ___ to Him.

cards.text: They offer a sacrifice to the LORD too. As for Jonah, he's in the sea, and trust me, friend, this story is NOT done.

findings.problem: The comparison doesn't match the action. In Jonah 1:2-3, Jonah hears the whole command and then runs. In the joke, you never pick up the boss's call, so you dodge hearing the job at all. 'Buying a plane ticket instead of picking up' is a different action from hearing the order and fleeing it.

rule.text: The everyday comparison must have the same action.

findings.problem: This card adds nothing new from the passage. The ship in danger (card 9), the sailors crying out to their gods (card 10) and Jonah's deep sleep (card 12) were all told or asked already, so the card is a recap with a joke on it. The joke also blends its everyday image with the Bible setting ('the snooze button on a hurricane').

rule.text: Every story card moves the baker forward through the passage. No recap cards.

findings.problem: The comparison (hitting the snooze button) is merged with the Bible setting (the storm, stretched into a hurricane) instead of standing as one everyday image.

rule.text: One image only. Never blend the comparison with the Bible setting.

findings.problem: 'Like a job interview in the middle of a storm' blends the everyday comparison (a job interview) with the Bible setting (the storm).

rule.text: One image only. Never blend the comparison with the Bible setting.

findings.problem: This story card is only a joke. Jonah's description of the LORD as the God who made the sea was already asked on card 5, so the card tells no part of the passage. The joke should ride on a card that moves the passage forward, such as card 8.

rule.text: Every story card tells part of the passage. Jokes ride along on those cards.

findings.problem: Card 14 already gave all of Jonah 1:15, so 'Calm.' tells nothing new and the card is only a joke. The joke also says the sea calmed quickly ('I've waited longer for an oven to cool off'), but Jonah 1:15 gives no time for how fast it grew calm.

rule.text: Every story card tells part of the passage. Jokes ride along on those cards.

findings.problem: The joke adds a time the text doesn't give: that the sea calmed fast.

rule.text: Times stay true. No time in the text means none added.

findings.problem: The 'story isn't over' line, 'trust me, friend, this story is NOT done,' nearly copies the doc's example line ('Trust me, friend, this story's not done.') instead of being a new line.

rule.text: The examples show the idea. Write your own line each time.
